system.description: Humans are restless, adaptable, and ambitious, making much of their brief lives and finding strength in one another.

lore.label: Summary
lore.text: Humans are restless, adaptable, and ambitious, making much of their brief lives and finding strength in one another.

lore.label: About
lore.text:
Humans are everywhere, and everywhere they are different. No other people spreads so far, argues so loudly, or reinvents itself so often. A human border town can change its laws, its faith, and its skyline inside a single generation; an elf who naps through a decade returns to find the maps redrawn. What humans lack in long memory they repay in momentum, and the other peoples watch them with a mix of admiration and alarm.

That restlessness is personal as much as cultural. A human feels the shortness of their years and answers it with ambition: one more field cleared, one more deal struck, one more mountain nobody sensible would climb. At their best, humans bind strangers into companies and companies into causes. At their worst, they burn through places, promises, and people the way they burn through years.

lore.label: If you want...
lore.text: If you want a character who can come from anywhere, get along with anyone, and refuse to stay in any lane, you should play a human.

lore.label: You Might...
lore.text:
• Chase a goal so hard that rest starts to feel like theft.
• Collect skills, contacts, and causes the way others collect coins.
• Assume any problem can be solved if you just find the right people for it.

lore.label: Others Probably...
lore.text:
• Envy how quickly you learn, adapt, and move on.
• Wonder what you are running from, or racing toward.
• Trust your knack for finding common ground, even between old enemies.

lore.label: Physical Description (at a glance)
lore.text: Humans are middling in most measures and wildly varied in all of them. They stand roughly five to six and a half feet tall, in every build from wiry to broad, with skin, hair, and eyes spanning every shade their homelands offer. What marks a human crowd is not a shared look but a shared motion: quick eyes, busy hands, and clothing that borrows freely from every neighbor they have ever traded with.

lore.label: Physical Description (life cycle)
lore.text: Humans reach physical adulthood around 15 years and are usually granted a place at the adults' table by 18, though every town draws that line differently. A human who avoids war, plague, and their own ambition can expect sixty to ninety years, and a rare few see a century. Their short season is the quiet engine of their character; humans plant orchards whose shade they will never sit in, and they know it.

lore.label: Society
lore.text:
Human society is less a single design than a permanent argument about what the design should be. Kingdoms, leagues, free towns, wandering companies: humans have tried them all, usually at the same time, usually within a week's ride of each other. Their gift is the joining of strangers. A human market will seat a dwarven smith beside an elven dyer and a gnomish clockmaker, and by closing time the three will share a ledger and a grudge against the harbormaster.

Because they invent themselves so freely, humans put enormous weight on names, oaths, and reputations, the few things that outlive them. A human's word, once given before witnesses, is a load-bearing wall; whole towns stand on webs of such promises. Breaking one is not just a sin but a kind of vandalism.

Humans honor their dead by continuing their projects. Workshops, farms, feuds, and half-built bridges pass from hand to hand like torches, and a human family can often recite what each generation added to the house even when they have forgotten the builders' faces.

lore.label: Beliefs
lore.text: Human belief runs hot and plural. One village keeps six shrines and hedges its bets at all of them; the next follows a single creed with terrifying focus. What is consistent is the human conviction that effort matters, that the world is unfinished, and that somebody, probably them, ought to get on with finishing it. Their prayers tend to be practical: strength for the harvest, luck for the crossing, courage for the morning.

lore.label: Popular Edicts
lore.text:
• Leave every place better than you found it.
• Keep your word once witnesses have heard it.
• Lift the newcomer; you were one once.

lore.label: Popular Anathemas
lore.text:
• Waste a year owed to the people who raised you.
• Break a promise made before witnesses.
• Let fear of failing keep you from beginning.

lore.label: Names
lore.text:
Human given names vary widely between families and homelands. Many human surnames preserve an ancestor’s occupation, carrying the memory of a workshop, livelihood, or useful skill through generations. A family named Cooper might have stopped making barrels centuries ago, yet still treasure the name.

Common given names Alden, Bram, Cassia, Doran, Elsbeth, Garron, Hale, Imre, Joss, Lysa, Mara, Oren, Sera, Tavin, Wren, Ysolde.

Common surnames Baker, Carter, Cooper, Fletcher, Mason, Miller, Roper, Tanner, Turner, Weaver.

Example names Alden Cooper, Cassia Fletcher, Elsbeth Weaver, Garron Mason, Lysa Carter, Tavin Roper.

system.specialAbility: You gain the Rally Aura: The first time each round an ally within 15 feet who can see you defends against an Attack with the Fear trait, they gain a +1 Situation bonus to that Defense check.

Serrovanians build trust through witnessed promises, careful records, and the conviction that a person should answer for their word.

lore.label: Summary
lore.text: Serrovanians build trust through witnessed promises, careful records, and the conviction that a person should answer for their word.

lore.label: About
lore.text:
Serrovane is a lowland order-state of cultivated fields, raised roads, and towns gathered around registry halls. Its ledgers are kept in triplicate, its agreements carry witnesses, and its disputes follow forms that everyone is expected to respect. A promise spoken casually may be forgotten. A promise entered into the record becomes something other people can build their lives upon.

People of many ancestries belong to this order. An elven witness, a dwarven magistrate, and a human challenger may disagree bitterly while trusting the same record. Serrovanians learn how to state a grievance, acknowledge an obligation, and offer a concession without surrendering their standing. They can be formidable negotiators: they know exactly what they have promised, and they expect you to know the same.

lore.label: If you want...
lore.text: If you want a character who takes promises seriously, understands the power of public reputation, and can turn a few carefully chosen words into a lasting obligation, choose Serrovane.

lore.label: You Might...
lore.text:
• Ask who witnessed an agreement before asking whether it was a good one.
• Carry copies of important promises, judgments, or introductions among your belongings.
• Insist on settling the terms of a contest before anyone draws a weapon.

lore.label: Others Probably...
lore.text:
• Trust you to remember an obligation long after everyone else has forgotten it.
• Find your careful questions reassuring, exhausting, or faintly threatening.
• Worry that an innocent remark might become a commitment in your hearing.

lore.label: Dress and Bearing
lore.text:
Serrovanian clothing favors orderly layers, durable fabrics, and visible signs of affiliation. Household colors, office badges, and witness cords help others recognize whom a person represents. Garments vary with ancestry, occupation, and means, but people generally take care that closures are secure and identifying marks remain legible.

Formal bearing matters as much as fine clothing. Standing to acknowledge a witness, leaving another speaker room to finish, and presenting a document with clean hands all communicate respect.

lore.label: Upbringing and Milestones
lore.text:
Children learn promises through ordinary responsibilities: returning borrowed tools, delivering messages accurately, and admitting when a task remains unfinished. Many households preserve a young person’s first independently witnessed obligation.

Public responsibility follows demonstrated judgment, with its timing shaped by ancestry and family custom. Taking an office, joining a household, completing an apprenticeship, and retiring from service are commonly marked by a formal acknowledgment of the duties being accepted or released.

lore.label: Society
lore.text:
Serrovanian institutions depend on recorded responsibilities. Officials swear to the limits of their offices, guilds preserve the terms of their charters, and households keep accounts of debts, inheritances, and obligations. Public scribes and witnesses are familiar figures in markets and village squares.

Formal challenge gives disputes an accepted shape. The grievance, the contest, and the consequences are declared before witnesses. Some challenges involve arms; others test skill, testimony, or the ability to substantiate a claim. Violence within accepted terms can be lawful. Breaking those terms threatens the trust that made the challenge possible.

This order has its cruelties. Wealth buys patient advocates, old records can preserve old injustices, and a precisely worded agreement can conceal an ugly intention. Serrovanians argue fiercely over whether justice lies in honoring the record or correcting what should never have been written into it.

lore.label: Beliefs
lore.text:
Serrovanians follow many faiths, but promises, testimony, and remembrance occupy an honored place across them. Shrines often witness marriages, reconciliations, and vows of service. An ancestor may be remembered through an obligation their descendants continue to uphold.

Mercy also has a recognized dignity. Publicly releasing someone from an oath can be an act of generosity remembered as long as the oath itself.

lore.label: Popular Edicts
lore.text:
• Keep your word when doing so becomes inconvenient.
• State your terms before the contest begins.
• Stand witness when another needs the truth recorded.

lore.label: Popular Anathemas
lore.text:
• Knowingly swear an oath you intend to break.
• Falsify a record entrusted to your care.
• Inflict punishment beyond the terms of an accepted challenge.

lore.label: Names
lore.text:
Many Serrovanian surnames take the form of a short promise: something a household declares it will uphold. These names are inherited, and families take particular pride in living up to them. Someone named Speaktrue can expect a lie to be remembered with unusual clarity.

People commonly retain given names from their family or ancestry. The surnames below are familiar Common translations of Serrovine names.

Common given names Cerran, Dovra, Ilyra, Maroven, Orven, Selka, Tavren, Veyra.

Common surnames Bearwitness, Holdfaith, Keepword, Speaktrue, Standfast.

Example names Cerran Keepword, Dovra Standfast, Ilyra Speaktrue, Maroven Bearwitness, Selka Holdfaith.

system.specialAbility:
You were raised in Serrovane.

You know the Common and Serrovine languages.

You gain a +1 Condition bonus to Diplomacy checks toward those who share the same Culture.

system.description: Reachers thrive where people and possibilities meet, building livelihoods through sharp observation, useful introductions, and bargains worth making again.

lore.label: Summary
lore.text: Reachers thrive where people and possibilities meet, building livelihoods through sharp observation, useful introductions, and bargains worth making again.

lore.label: About
lore.text:
Kestrel Reach spreads across a wide river delta, where channels divide around crowded islands and trade-towns rise above the floodwater. Six languages may be spoken along a single dock, with three more heard by evening. Boats bring unfamiliar goods, travelers bring unfamiliar customs, and someone is always looking for a person who understands both.

Reachers grow accustomed to difference early. An elven shipwright, a dwarven grain factor, and a human ferryman may share a neighborhood, a business venture, and a running argument about harbor fees. Local knowledge means knowing how people prefer to be approached, which courtesies matter to them, and whom they trust to make an introduction. A good broker can accomplish with an afternoon’s conversation what an armed company might spend a season making worse.

lore.label: If you want...
lore.text: If you want a character who is comfortable among unfamiliar faces, always listening for an opportunity, and rarely without someone they could ask for help, choose Kestrel Reach.

lore.label: You Might...
lore.text:
Learn a few useful words whenever you encounter a new language.
Introduce yourself by naming someone the other person already knows.
Look for what each side needs before deciding that a dispute cannot be settled.

lore.label: Others Probably...
lore.text:
Expect you to know a useful contact in almost any port.
Wonder whether your friendly questions are leading toward a proposal.
Rely on you to notice the custom, omission, or hidden cost they overlooked.

lore.label: Dress and Bearing
lore.text:
Reach clothing reflects crowded docks, changeable weather, and goods arriving from distant places. Practical layers, secure pockets, broad hats, and garments kept clear of ropes are common. Fabrics and ornaments travel freely between communities, adapted to each wearer’s build and family traditions.

Reachers often display a token of their trade, vessel, or trading house where an acquaintance can recognize it. Greeting gestures vary between neighborhoods, and knowing which one to offer can make a warmer introduction than expensive clothes.

lore.label: Upbringing and Milestones
lore.text:
Young Reachers learn by carrying messages, helping with household business, and accompanying experienced relatives through markets and landing places. They are taught to notice who has spoken, who has been overlooked, and whether everyone understands the same terms.

A first independently completed bargain or entrusted journey often marks growing responsibility. Its importance lies in returning with the agreement fulfilled and the other party willing to deal with the household again. These milestones follow readiness and circumstance across the Reach’s many ancestries.

lore.label: Society
lore.text:
The delta depends on cooperation that extends beyond individual towns. Ferrymen need maintained channels, merchants need dependable warehouses, and everyone needs the flood banks to hold. Neighborhood associations, trading houses, craft guilds, and harbor officials overlap in a web of favors and competing responsibilities.

Reputation moves quickly along the waterways. A generous settlement can bring business from three towns away; a cheated customer can arrive ahead of you wherever you hoped to trade next. Brokers earn their standing by remembering details, protecting confidences, and finding terms that people will actually honor.

The Reach’s friendliness can conceal hard boundaries. Established houses sometimes keep profitable routes among themselves, and an introduction may matter more than an excellent offer. Reachers admire people who open opportunities for others, but they also know how easily a well-connected few can decide who gets a place at the table.

lore.label: Beliefs
lore.text:
Reach shrines welcome travelers, returning crews, and families whose traditions came from elsewhere. River spirits, ancestral patrons, and gods of craft, fortune, and safe passage all receive offerings.

Many Reachers regard hospitality as an obligation that travels. Someone shelters a stranger today because another household may shelter their own kin tomorrow. Gifts, favors, and acts of kindness create relationships whose value cannot always be entered into an account.

lore.label: Popular Edicts
lore.text:
Learn how to greet people on their own terms.
Give the other party a reason to trade with you again.
Share a useful introduction when it costs you little.

lore.label: Popular Anathemas
lore.text:
Abuse the protection offered to a guest.
Conceal a danger that makes an agreement impossible to fulfill.
Betray a confidence entrusted to you as a broker.

lore.label: Names
lore.text:
Reach surnames often come from waterways and shoreline features. A name may remember the bank where a household built its first home, the channel its boats worked, or the landing from which its members scattered across the world. Families carry these names inland long after the river itself has become a distant memory.

Given names mingle freely across languages and ancestries. The surnames below are commonly used in their Common forms.

Common given names Avi, Dena, Jori, Kes, Lio, Mira, Neris, Orren, Savi, Tavi.

Common surnames Broadwater, Lowbank, Northbank, Reedbank, Siltwater, Stillwater, Three-Tides, Willowbend.

Example names Avi Northbank, Dena Willowbend, Jori Reedbank, Mira Three-Tides, Neris Stillwater, Tavi Lowbank.

system.specialAbility:
You were raised in Kestrel Reach.

You know the Common and Reachspeak languages.

You gain a +1 Condition bonus to Diplomacy checks toward those who share the same Culture.
You become Trained in Athletics and in Acrobatics, and you become Trained in a relevant Lore of your choice.
system.description: In a circus or on the streets, you earned your pay by performing as an acrobat. You might have turned to adventuring when the money dried up, or simply decided to put your skills to better use.

system.specialAbility: You become Trained in Athletics and in Intimidation, and you become Trained in a relevant Lore of your choice.
system.description: You served in somebody's army: a levy, a free company, a city watch that saw real fighting. You learned the drill, the marching, and the waiting, and you learned what a line looks like just before it breaks.

system.specialAbility: You become Trained in Guile and in Stealth, and you become Trained in a relevant Lore of your choice.
system.description: You made your living outside the law, whether by picking pockets, running contraband, or talking your way through doors that were meant to stay shut. You still know who to ask, and which questions never to.

system.specialAbility: Sneak Attack: +1d6 precision damage vs. Off-Guard foes, rising to +2d6 at Expert, +3d6 at Master, and +4d6 at Legendary.
system.description: Grants Training in Stealth, and 8 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.

system.specialAbility: Rage ❶: Temporary Vigor equal to your level + Might, +2 melee damage, −1 Evade, and you are Heedless while it lasts. The damage rises to +4 at Expert, +6 at Master, +8 at Legendary.
system.description: Grants Training in Athletics, and 12 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.

system.specialAbility: Panache: held on a critical Strike, a Feint, or a Demoralize; +1 Situation to Evade and +1 ft to your Speeds while you hold it (Speed +2 ft at Expert, Evade +2 at Master, Speed +3 ft at Legendary).
system.description: Grants Training in Acrobatics, and 10 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.

system.specialAbility: Mark Prey ❶: +1d8 precision damage the first time each round you Hit your prey (2d8 at Expert, 3d8 at Master, 4d8 at Legendary), and you always know roughly where it is within 60 feet.
system.description: Grants Training in Awareness, and 10 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.

system.specialAbility: Drilled: Weapon Familiarity free; treat your Melee or Ranged Proficiency Bonus as 2 higher with that Weapon Group; and you may take Reactive Strike without being Expert in Melee.
system.description: Grants Training in Athletics, and 10 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.

system.specialAbility: Spellshaping: once per round, add ❶ to a Cast you know to extend its range by 5 feet, or to move one square of its area; your first Calling also trains you in a magical discipline.
system.description: Grants Training in Guile, and 6 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.

system.specialAbility: Blood Price: once per round, lose 1 + the discipline's Damage Dice in Vigor as you declare a damaging Cast; if it Hits, one creature takes that much more.
system.description: Grants Training in Athletics, and 8 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.

system.specialAbility: Death Echo: once per round, when a living creature within 15 feet takes a Wound or becomes Spent, hold an Echo; spend it before a Strike or damaging Cast for +2 damage on a Hit.
system.description: Grants Training in Awareness, and 6 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.

system.specialAbility: Call Manifestation ❷: one 1-foot manifestation within 6 feet, lasting the encounter; Command ❶ it to Move or make a 1d4 Zoned Strike. It vanishes on a Hit.
system.description: Grants Training in Awareness, and 6 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.

system.specialAbility: Spellbound Edge ❶: your next Deliberate Melee Strike deals a known spell's damage type instead of its own. Needs Melee and a magical discipline.
system.description: Grants Training in Athletics, and 8 Opening Vigor, added once if it is your first Calling.
